en: The encampment of everyone he encountered,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: I shall be Chyng Temir.
The eighteen thousand worlds,
If he gathered and seized them wholesale,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: I shall drive them on and exact tribute.
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: If my fury rises and I strike with a curse,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: Would the black mountain not be shattered?
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: If a stark command comes from the khan,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: Would its onslaught not find them?
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: When the Mongols stood in Beijing,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: Would he not exact tribute from a whole world?
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: If you stiffen in anger,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: The four corners of the world,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: The five quarters you have marked out,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: Would they not be smashed to pieces?
When I become Chyng Temir,
Scorching until the sands were swept up,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: When rejoicing, he was no mere common man,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: The valleys shook and mountains fell,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: My valiant one knew it.
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: As the age approached its end,
Thus he came to Kakan,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: Saying the enemy would not take what was given,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: He was destined for great dominion.
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: Saying this, Chyng Temir,
Angrily gathered an army,
When he gathered troops, he gathered a multitude,
Those younger than fifty-five,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: Let not a single old soul remain,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: Those who had passed eighteen,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: The roll of the young men,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: Saying not one youth should remain behind,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: Kakan, root and branch,
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: He gathered them all together.
From the elder side came grievous slaughter.
uncertainty_note: Provisional reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or word division; preserve for later high-confidence collation.

en: He had cast the people into a dispute.
uncertainty_note: The causative verb is written in a nonstandard form and is provisionally normalized only in translation.

en: Their wits bewildered, their heads aching,
He had cast the people into turmoil,
He did not stand by and watch in vain,
uncertainty_note: The final verb is a manuscript form provisionally read турбаттыр.

en: An extraordinary upheaval, a great conflict,
The people were ruined and the nation grieved,
An extraordinary affliction, a great conflict,
The people rose and began to assemble.
uncertainty_note: жыйышатыр is retained as written and may represent a nonstandard progressive form.

en: Of what the Kalmyk had given,
uncertainty_note: The short line is syntactically dependent on the following line.

en: Of what had long been increasing since ancient times,
uncertainty_note: Абалтан молоп is a provisional reading of difficult handwriting.

en: The Kyrgyz asked grimly.
uncertainty_note: The adjective жаман may function adverbially here.

en: A wrathful scourge began.
uncertainty_note: кээр is a provisional reading of the middle word.

en: The people cried out and tumult arose,
When they looked, nothing caught the eye,
The people stirred in a great upheaval,
uncertainty_note: The final noun is provisionally read төңкөр.

en: Its sorrow could not be discerned,
They gathered an army for the contest,
uncertainty_note: Керидешке is a provisional reading.

en: They gathered the whole host in great numbers.
Together they stood in Kongol,
uncertainty_note: The place or descriptive word Коңголдо is uncertain.

en: The affliction that threw the people into panic,
How the True Lord had measured it,
uncertainty_note: The opening words are difficult and provisionally read Чымалын кандай.

en: Such was the command he gave.
The great Chinese nation cried aloud,
They had witnessed their khan’s wrath,
Stricken by its warrior,
uncertainty_note: эсинген is a provisional reading.

en: The brave Eren, Khan Esen,
uncertainty_note: The sequence may contain the epithet эрен and the name Эсен кан.

en: Sat burdened with worry,
While the people cried out in distress,
As he was about to take up his decree,
uncertainty_note: The final word is provisionally read алырдачы.

en: His wrath became known to the people,
A merciless ordeal began,
uncertainty_note: жадал is a provisional reading of a difficult word.

en: Even their livestock were plundered,
All the people found no refuge,
uncertainty_note: The final phrase is provisionally read коргон таппаптыр.

en: Asking what this khan’s decree might be,
The populace cowered in fear,
uncertainty_note: The final two words are difficult and provisionally read коркуп жырданып.

en: The wise among them marveled,
The witless did not understand,
Bewildered by milk and kumis,
uncertainty_note: The final word looks like таңданып, but its sense with milk and kumis is unresolved; both transcription and literal English remain provisional.

en: The people stood pale with longing.
Chyng Tengir was indeed a mighty lord,
Kakanchy and Beijing were his support,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript appears to read бел (support), not бек (lord); the elliptical construction remains provisional.

en: Not merely Beijing, but the whole world—
The time had come for him to rule it,
uncertainty_note: Manuscript reads Соро; understood as a form of суроо (rule/govern). Final noun is кези (time), not көзү (eye).

en: A true mainstay of the world,
The time had come for him to become one.
A sage, accomplished in stratagems,
Even the black scourge could not escape
The noble hero Tengir.
uncertainty_note: Manuscript ending appears баатырдан, whereas the printed counterpart has баатырдын. Manuscript variant retained.

en: Envoys who came forth before him,
uncertainty_note: Manuscript reads чыккан, whereas the printed counterpart has чыкты; variant retained.

en: Inspectors with imposing bearing,
Judges who could tell from outward signs,
Spies who roamed the land,
Those who went about by cunning,
Those who knew the measure of a people,
Those who loaded burdens onto camels,
Their gold and silver,
Those who traveled in trade to sell it,
Of the Kyrgyz in Ala-Too,
Those who drew out their inner secrets,
Those who knew the extent of their cunning,
Those who kindled discord among them,
How great their strength and resources were,
Those who watched and studied from outside,
The keenest judge among those observers,
The judge Zhelzhetpes had arrived,
The strength and resources of the Kyrgyz,
He had assessed, observing their people.
From the inspector who roamed the land,
uncertainty_note: Final noun appears ченчиден (from an inspector); case/ending remains provisional.

en: From the dark eye of calamity,
From the dark eye of the scourge,
With doors open and belts loosened,
The dear people living at ease,
Making them move as though within a bend,
uncertainty_note: First phrase provisionally read Кайыр ичиндей. Its referent and idiom are unresolved; English is a literal tentative rendering, not a recovered confident sense.
